research_problem: LLM tool learning assumes static APIs; when deployed APIs change (names, parameters, response formats) LLMs keep invoking outdated APIs and fail
technical_approach: ToolEVO: MCTS-based active exploration of a dynamic tool environment with self-reflection on invocation errors and a tool-update action that rewrites API usage in the prompt after deprecation errors; successful trajectories (~30k) used for SFT of Llama3-8B/Qwen2-7B; ToolQA-D benchmark built by GPT-4-modified ToolQA APIs (in-domain and OOD variants)
primary_contribution: First framework and benchmark (ToolQA-D) for LLM adaptation to tool/API variability
dataset_benchmark: ToolQA-D: 7 ToolQA domains, Easy/Hard, ~6k training samples each, 700/730 test; three API sets (Pc, Ps_in, Ps_OOD)
evaluation_metrics: Task success rate per domain and difficulty
baselines: GPT-3.5/4/4o/4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Llama3 and Qwen2 series (incl. 70B/72B), Static-SFT
key_findings: Tool variability degrades all models, Static-SFT most (repeats deprecated calls); ToolEVO 7-8B matches Static-SFT in static setting and beats Static-SFT and 72B models in dynamic and OOD settings (best proprietary OOD average 60.2 easy / 32.1 hard); parameter changes hurt more than name changes, response format changes least; self-reflection ablation causes largest drop
author_limitations: ToolEVO still makes invocation errors with new tools and misreads responses; SFT only, no preference learning; preliminary exploration
analyst_limitations: Synthetic semantic-preserving renames do not reflect real breaking/behavioral API changes; deprecation messages name the replacement API (unrealistically helpful); small synthetic ToolQA domains not real web APIs; no documentation-retrieval baseline; single greedy run without statistics; no threats section
reproducibility: Code on GitHub; GPT-4-generated modifications; open base models
suggested_extensions: Benchmark from real OpenAPI/library evolution histories incl. behavioral changes and uninformative errors; spec-diff/changelog-aware agents vs MCTS; MCP tool schema evolution robustness; machine-readable deprecation governance for agent consumers; preference/continual learning
evidence_location: Problem p.1-3; method p.3-5; ToolQA-D p.5-6; results p.7-8 Tables 2-4; analysis p.8-9; ablation p.9-10; appendix error analysis
integrity: MCTS formulas partly lost; result tables column-split so ToolEVO averages not fully recoverable; figures missing
